# Madlanga Commission | Witness H's testimony to be heard behind closed doors amid safety concerns

[![Follow IOL on Google News](/_next/static/media/iol-google-news-follow.6c774fa8.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAqIggKIhxDQklTRHdnTWFnc0tDV2x2YkM1amJ5NTZZU2dBUAE?ceid=ZA:en&oc=3")

![](https://iol-prod.appspot.com/image/674e51cd7977123ce66d8889a5342560137b70b5=w700)

Proceedings at the Madlanga Commission will include closed-door sessions as a crime intelligence officer gives evidence.

Image: Oupa Mokoena / Independent Newspapers

The Madlanga Commission of Inquiry resolved to hear the testimony of a crime intelligence officer known as [Witness H](https://iol.co.za/news/crime-and-courts/2026-05-05-witness-seeks-closed-door-testimony-at-madlanga-commission-over-cocaine-stolen-from-kzn-hawks-offices/) [](https://iol.co.za/news/crime-and-courts/2026-05-05-witness-seeks-closed-door-testimony-at-madlanga-commission-over-cocaine-stolen-from-kzn-hawks-offices/)behind closed doors for safety reasons.

The witness is scheduled to testify before the commission on Friday, May 8, 2026, and will be in camera with no video or audio feed to the public.

The witness supplied a supporting affidavit on Tuesday to motivate for an order directing that the testimony be heard in camera. 

The supporting affidavit was deposed by Thabiso Lesufi, an attorney representing the witness who wished to remain anonymous.

The background to the application arises from hearings that commenced on Tuesday regarding a major drug theft of 541 bricks of cocaine valued at R200 million from Hawks premises in Port Shepstone, KwaZulu-Natal (KZN).

Major-General Hendrik Flynn, Component Head for Serious Organised Crime at the SAPS Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation (DPCI), told the commission that the theft of cocaine from the Hawks premises was intentional.

The commission heard that 547 kg of mandrax had been stored at Isipingo Police Station’s SAP13 store 16 months earlier, yet there was suddenly insufficient space to store 541 kg of cocaine. As a result, the cocaine was taken to a DPCI storage facility in Port Shepstone. It was not stored at Maydon Wharf, Brighton Beach, Umbilo, or Durban Central.

According to Flynn’s testimony, KwaZulu-Natal Hawks head Major-General Lesetja Senona did not follow prescripts for handling the keys to the Port Shepstone warehouse, where the cocaine bricks went missing following a mysterious burglary in 2021.

![](https://iol-prod.appspot.com/image/6016f70224aa68fd6fb19d842481501d307b9c43=w700)

Witness requests confidential testimony in Madlanga Commission cocaine case.

Image: Oupa Mokoena / Independent Newspapers

The anonymous witness serves as a pivotal figure in the investigation team, reportedly possessing extensive knowledge vital to the inquiry.

Their anticipated testimony is not only set to address the seizure of the drugs at Durban harbour but will also delve into the processes surrounding the storage and handling of the seized narcotics, along with insights pertaining to the ongoing investigations into the Port Shepstone theft.

According to the affidavit, the sensitivity of the evidence warrants utmost confidentiality. The witness is prepared to discuss information pertaining to investigative findings, policing methods, and details about confidential informants that have not been disclosed to the public.

“Public disclosure of such information at this stage would risk alerting suspects, facilitating the destruction of evidence, compromising investigative strategies, and exposing individuals who have provided critical information. The investigations are interconnected, and disclosure in respect of one investigation would create a real risk of exposing details of other ongoing investigations,” read the affidavit.

“In light of the sensitive nature of the evidence, the advanced but incomplete status of the investigations, and the need to protect witnesses, informants, and the integrity of ongoing and future prosecutions, it is further requested that the identity of the witness be protected and that the statement and transcripts of the testimony not be subject to public disclosure,” the affidavit further stated.

MADLANGA COMMISSION TO CONTINUE FOCUS ON SEIZURE AND THEFT OF DRUGS AHEAD OF SECOND INTERIM REPORT

STATEMENT BY JEREMY MICHAELS, SPOKESPERSON OF THE JUDICIAL COMMISSION OF INQUIRY INTO CRIMINALITY, POLITICAL INTERFERENCE AND CORRUPTION IN THE CRIMINAL JUSTICE SYSTEM

The Madlanga Commission’s hearings in the week ahead (11-15 May 2026) will continue to focus on drug seizures by South African law enforcement agencies, as well as the handling and theft or disappearance of narcotic substances in KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng.

This is a continuation of the testimony of several witnesses last week, including the in-camera evidence of Witness H on Friday 8 May 2026.

This is the last week of public hearings before the Commission breaks from 18 May 2026 to focus on its second Interim Report, which is due to be delivered to President Cyril Ramaphosa on 29 May 2026.

Mr President Ramaphosa and SAPS Senior Officials,

I respectfully request a clear and transparent directive on the way forward regarding the 2025/26 SAPS recruitment application.

Last year, posts were advertised and selection processes were carried out in almost all provinces, reaching the final stages. Many young South Africans were raised with hope after completing several recruitment stages. However, there has been no communication or progress, particularly concerning medical assessments.

The **Government of South Africa**, or **South African Government**, is the [national government](/wiki/Government "Government") of the [Republic of South Africa](/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa"), a [parliamentary republic](/wiki/Parliamentary_republic "Parliamentary republic") with a three-tier system of government and an independent [judiciary](/wiki/Judiciary "Judiciary"), operating in a [parliamentary system](/wiki/Parliamentary_system "Parliamentary system"). Legislative authority is held by the [Parliament of South Africa](/wiki/Parliament_of_South_Africa "Parliament of South Africa"). Executive authority is vested in the [President of South Africa](/wiki/President_of_South_Africa "President of South Africa") who is head of state and head of government, and their Cabinet. The President is elected by the Parliament to serve a fixed term.

South Africa's government differs from those of other [Commonwealth](/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations") nations. The national, provincial and local levels of government all have [legislative](/wiki/Legislature "Legislature") and executive authority in their own spheres, and are defined in the South African [Constitution](/wiki/Constitution_of_South_Africa "Constitution of South Africa") as "distinctive, interdependent and interrelated".

Operating at both national and provincial levels ("domes") are advisory bodies drawn from South Africa's traditional leaders. It is a stated intention in the Constitution that the country be run on a system of cooperative governance.

The national [government](/wiki/Government "Government") is composed of three inter-connected branches; the legislature (parliament, consisting of the [National Assembly](/wiki/National_Assembly_of_South_Africa "National Assembly of South Africa") and the [National Council of Provinces](/wiki/National_Council_of_Provinces "National Council of Provinces")), the executive (the [President](/wiki/President_of_South_Africa "President of South Africa"), who is both [Head of State](/wiki/Head_of_State "Head of State") and [Head of Government](/wiki/Head_of_Government "Head of Government")), and the judiciary (the [Constitutional Court](/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_South_Africa "Constitutional Court of South Africa"), the [Supreme Court of Appeal](/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Appeal_of_South_Africa "Supreme Court of Appeal of South Africa"), and the [High Court](/wiki/High_Court_of_South_Africa "High Court of South Africa")).

All bodies of the South African Government are subject to the rule of the Constitution, which is the supreme law in South Africa.

The [Parliament of the Republic of South Africa](/wiki/Parliament_of_South_Africa "Parliament of South Africa") is [South Africa](/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa")'s [legislature](/wiki/Legislature "Legislature"). It is located in [Cape Town](/wiki/Cape_Town "Cape Town"); the country's legislative [capital](/wiki/Capital_city "Capital city").

Under the present [Constitution of South Africa](/wiki/Constitution_of_South_Africa "Constitution of South Africa"), the [bicameral](/wiki/Bicameralism "Bicameralism") Parliament comprises a [National Assembly](/wiki/National_Assembly_\(South_Africa\) "National Assembly (South Africa)") and a [National Council of Provinces](/wiki/National_Council_of_Provinces "National Council of Provinces").[\[2\]](#cite_note-2)[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) The current [twenty-eighth Parliament](/wiki/28th_South_African_Parliament "28th South African Parliament") was first convened on 14 June 2024.

From 1910 to 1994, members of Parliament were elected chiefly by the South African [white minority](/wiki/Whites_in_South_Africa "Whites in South Africa"). The first elections with universal suffrage were held in [1994](/wiki/South_African_general_election,_1994 "South African general election, 1994").

Both chambers held their meetings in the [Houses of Parliament, Cape Town](/wiki/Houses_of_Parliament,_Cape_Town "Houses of Parliament, Cape Town") that were built 1875–1884. A [fire](/wiki/2022_Parliament_of_South_Africa_fire "2022 Parliament of South Africa fire") broke out within the buildings in early January 2022, destroying the session room of the National Assembly. It was decided that, during construction work at Parliament, the National Assembly would temporarily meet at the [Good Hope Chamber](/wiki/Good_Hope_Chamber "Good Hope Chamber").[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

The [President](/wiki/President_of_South_Africa "President of South Africa"), [Deputy President](/wiki/Deputy_President_of_South_Africa "Deputy President of South Africa") and the Ministers of the South African Government make up the [executive branch](/wiki/Executive_branch "Executive branch") of the national government. The president is elected by parliament from its members.

## Judicial

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Government_of_South_Africa&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Judicial")\]

Main article: [Judiciary of South Africa](/wiki/Judiciary_of_South_Africa "Judiciary of South Africa")

The third branch of the national government is an independent judiciary. The judicial branch interprets the laws, using as a basis the laws as enacted and explanatory statements made in the Legislature during the enactment. The legal system is based on [Roman-Dutch law](/wiki/Roman-Dutch_law "Roman-Dutch law") and [English common law](/wiki/English_common_law "English common law") and accepts compulsory [ICJ](/wiki/International_Court_of_Justice "International Court of Justice") jurisdiction, with reservations. The constitution's bill of rights provides for due process including the right to a [fair](/wiki/Fair_trial "Fair trial"), [public trial](/wiki/Public_trial "Public trial") within a reasonable time.

The nine [provinces of South Africa](/wiki/Provinces_of_South_Africa "Provinces of South Africa") are governed by [provincial governments](/wiki/Provincial_governments_of_South_Africa "Provincial governments of South Africa") which form the second layer of government, between the national government and the [municipalities](/wiki/Municipalities_of_South_Africa "Municipalities of South Africa"). The provincial governments are established, and their structure defined, by [Chapter Six](/wiki/Chapter_Six_of_the_Constitution_of_South_Africa "Chapter Six of the Constitution of South Africa") of the [Constitution of South Africa](/wiki/Constitution_of_South_Africa "Constitution of South Africa").

The provincial governments are structured according to a [parliamentary system](/wiki/Parliamentary_system "Parliamentary system") in which the executive is dependent on and accountable to the legislature. In each province the [provincial legislature](/wiki/Provincial_legislature_\(South_Africa\) "Provincial legislature (South Africa)") is directly elected by [proportional representation](/wiki/Proportional_representation "Proportional representation"), and the legislature in turn elects one of its members as [Premier](/wiki/Premier_\(South_Africa\) "Premier (South Africa)") to head the executive. The Premier appoints an [Executive Council](/wiki/Executive_Council_\(South_Africa\) "Executive Council (South Africa)") (a cabinet), consisting of members of the legislature, to administer the various [departments](/wiki/Government_department "Government department") of the provincial administration.

The powers of the provincial governments are circumscribed by the national constitution, which limits them to certain listed "functional areas". In some areas the provincial governments' powers are concurrent with those of the national government, while in other areas the provincial governments have exclusive powers. The constitution prescribes a principle of "co-operative government" whereby the various layers of government must co-ordinate their actions and legislation; it also lays down a series of rules for resolving conflicts between national and provincial legislation.

## Local government

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Government_of_South_Africa&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Local government")\]

Main article: [Municipalities of South Africa](/wiki/Municipalities_of_South_Africa "Municipalities of South Africa")

[Local government](/wiki/Local_government "Local government") in South Africa consists of **municipalities** of various types. The largest [metropolitan areas](/wiki/Metropolitan_areas "Metropolitan areas") are governed by [metropolitan municipalities](/wiki/Metropolitan_municipality_\(South_Africa\) "Metropolitan municipality (South Africa)"), while the rest of the country[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) is divided into [district municipalities](/wiki/District_municipality_\(South_Africa\) "District municipality (South Africa)"), each of which consists of several [local municipalities](/wiki/Local_municipality_\(South_Africa\) "Local municipality (South Africa)"). After the [municipal election of 18 May 2011](/wiki/South_African_municipal_election,_2011 "South African municipal election, 2011") there were eight metropolitan municipalities, 44 district municipalities and 226 local municipalities.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

Municipalities are governed by [municipal councils](/wiki/Municipal_council "Municipal council") which are elected every five years. The councils of metropolitan and local municipalities are elected by a system of [mixed-member proportional representation](/wiki/Mixed-member_proportional_representation "Mixed-member proportional representation"), while the councils of district municipalities are partly elected by proportional representation and partly appointed by the councils of the constituent local municipalities.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

## Opposition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Government_of_South_Africa&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Opposition")\]

In each legislative body, the party or coalition of parties holding a majority of seats forms the government. The largest party not in the government is recognised as the official opposition.
